messages.subject: Plot Rendering Differences
parts:
I have noticed that plots will render differently within a browser depedning on where the app is launched from.
For example:
  1. Plot rendered by calling the app on the local computer
    • Lines between points are rendered clearly
  2. Plot rendered by calling app via server
    • Lines between points are barely visible
I have noted this regardless of browser (IE or Firefox). Any ideas on how to correct this?

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Plot Rendering Differences
parts:
It will depend on what platform the app is running on. Here are the default behaviors for different platforms:

* Mac: Points, lines, and text are antialiased.
* Linux: Points, lines, and text are antialiased, except for point shapes 16-18. (The default point shape for ggplot2 is 16.) Point centers are not aligned to the pixel grid, so they will have different, strange shapes.
* Windows: no antialiasing for points, lines, or text. Point centers will be aligned to the pixel grid, so they'll be consistent in shape.

It looks to me like your first image was created on Windows, and the second one was created on Linux. It also looks like you are using very thin vertical lines between the points -- on Windows, since there's no antialiasing, they'll be "expanded" to be one pixel wide, whereas on Linux (and Mac), lines that are thinner than one pixel will simply appear lighter, because of the antialiasing.

Fortunately, it is possible to get antialiasing on all objects. The CairoPNG() function from the Cairo package can be used for fully antialiased PNG output, and if you run install.packages('Cairo'), Shiny will automatically use it in renderPlot().

-Winston
